label: Woffle: What Is Algebraic Geometry
notes: Open the prologue. This informal chapter sets the scene before any formal definitions arrive. The deck follows printed pages 11 through 18 and explains, in plain terms, what algebraic geometry studies, why polynomial equations and their solution sets sit at its heart, and how the dictionary between algebra and geometry organizes the whole subject.

label: Polynomials and Their Zero Sets
notes: Start from the basic object: a system of polynomial equations and the set of points where they vanish. Lines, conics, and surfaces are all zero sets of polynomials. The geometry of these sets and the algebra of the polynomials defining them are two sides of one coin, and the course studies them together.

label: The Algebra-Geometry Dictionary
notes: Preview the central dictionary: geometric objects correspond to algebraic ones. Varieties match ideals, points match maximal ideals, and maps between varieties match homomorphisms of coordinate rings. This translation lets us solve geometric problems with algebra and interpret algebraic facts geometrically, the recurring strategy of the entire book.

label: Examples That Guide the Theory
notes: Survey the concrete examples that motivate the abstractions to come: plane conics, cubic curves and their group law, and the famous twenty-seven lines on a cubic surface. These hands-on cases, studied first, show why the general machinery is worth building and keep the theory anchored to vivid, computable geometry.

label: Why and How We Proceed
notes: Explain the spirit of the course: learn by playing with explicit curves and surfaces before formalizing. Reid's plan moves from plane curves to the category of affine varieties and then to applications. The emphasis throughout is on geometric intuition supported by just enough commutative algebra to make arguments precise.

label: Recap
notes: Close the prologue. Algebraic geometry studies zero sets of polynomials, the algebra-geometry dictionary translates between equations and shapes, and vivid examples like conics, cubics, and the cubic surface motivate everything. With the scene set, Chapter 01 begins the formal study by playing with plane conics.
